page: Microsoft Azure ND96asr_v4 is a high-density GPU-accelerated virtual machine tailored for distributed artificial intelligence, deep learning training, and intensive scientific computing. Powered by an x86_64 AMD processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server provides 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 900.0 GB of system memory, delivering approximately 9.38 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Acceleration is anchored by 8 NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs providing a combined total of 320 GB of video memory. To satisfy high data ingestion rates during training passes, the configuration incorporates 10,794 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The platform also includes RDMA network capabilities and support for Azure Premium Storage.

Given the substantial resource allocation across enterprise accelerators, large system memory, and multi-terabyte local NVMe capacity, this instance occupies an upper-tier resource profile built specifically for parallel execution. With zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, it is intended for deployment within secure virtual networks and compute clusters. It is optimized for large-scale deep neural network training, high-performance computing, and parallel simulation pipelines.
